At 3 p.m., the team finds a bug in the fraud check that has been live since 2. In a queue (RabbitMQ, SQS), the message is removed when the consumer finishes. In Kafka, the topic is a log: reading doesn't delete, and each consumer keeps only the offset of the next message. Once the bug is fixed, a seek moves the offset back and the consumer re-reads from there. The log deletes by the configured retention, and reprocessing repeats the effect: the consumer has to be idempotent.

Have you ever had to reprocess a queue? Tell me in the comments.

Sources: Apache Kafka 4.4, RabbitMQ (Streams) and Amazon SQS documentation. Part 2 of 4 of the Kafka series.

The author's voice is cloned with AI. Animations made for this video; fictional app, services and orders.
